title: Rome cites John 16 and John 21: much Jesus said and did went unwritten
source_text: II. Primum igitur ut probent multa esse Christi & Apostolorum dogmata, atque instituta quae sacris literis comprehensa non sunt, & tamen apud fideles authoritatem eandem obtinere debent ac illa quae scripta sunt, proferunt verba Christi Joan. 16. ubi discipulos suos alloquens, ait, Adhuc multa habeo vobis dicere, sed non potestis portare modo. Cui loco jungunt ea quae leguntur ultimo cap. ejus Evangelii, Sunt autem & alia multa quae fecit Jesus: quae, si scribantur per singula, nec ipsum arbitror mundum capere posse eos qui scribendi sunt, libros. Constat ergo, inquiunt, multa Dominum fecisse & dixisse, quae non sunt scripta. Nam illos libros qui extant una manus capere potest, Joannes autem dicit totum mundum non posse capere libros qui scribendi essent. Et praeterea illa quae promittebat Dominus se dicturum loco citato, dixit haud dubie post resurrectionem suam, ut colligi potest ex Actorum capite primo, ubi testatur Lucas Dominum post resurrectionem per quadraginta dies apparuisse discipulis, & ipsis locutum fuisse de iis quae pertinent ad regnum Dei. At de gestis & verbis Domini post resurrectionem paucissima scripserunt Evangelistae. Non autem est ullo modo credibile Apostolos, qui illa viderant aut audierant, non tradidisse Ecclesiis. Nec enim invidi, aut obliviosi erant, ut nollent, aut non possent ea dicere.
pass_a_gloss: First therefore, that they may prove there are many dogmas and institutions of Christ and the Apostles which are not comprehended in the sacred letters, and yet ought to obtain the same authority among the faithful as those which are written, they bring forward the words of Christ in John 16, where addressing his disciples he says, I still have many things to say to you, but you cannot bear them now. To which place they join those which are read in the last chapter of his Gospel, But there are also many other things which Jesus did: which, if they were written one by one, I suppose that even the world itself could not contain the books that would be written. Therefore it is clear, they say, that the Lord did and said many things which are not written. For those books which exist one hand can hold, but John says the whole world could not contain the books that would have to be written. And besides, those things which the Lord promised he would say in the place cited, he said without doubt after his resurrection, as can be gathered from the first chapter of Acts, where Luke testifies that the Lord after the resurrection appeared to the disciples for forty days, and spoke to them of the things that pertain to the kingdom of God. But of the deeds and words of the Lord after the resurrection the Evangelists wrote very little. And it is in no way credible that the Apostles, who had seen or heard those things, did not hand them on to the Churches. For they were neither envious nor forgetful, so as to be unwilling or unable to say them.
pass_b_english: Rome opens with John 16: I still have many things to say — you cannot bear them now.
They add John 21: the world could not hold books of all Jesus did.
Acts 1: forty days of kingdom teaching after the resurrection, yet the Gospels write little of it.
So, they say, much apostolic teaching must live in unwritten tradition.
